title: Ella Langley Shares a Thoughtful New Song for the Next 'Hunger Games' Film
summary:
Some songs sound like a quiet evening after a long day. Ella Langley's new song, "Here Then We're Gone," is one of them. The country singer shared the gentle, acoustic track on Friday, November 13, for the soundtrack of the upcoming film The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

Langley wrote the song with Aaron Raitiere and Ernest, and Dave Cobb produced it. Its lyrics look back at someone who is gone and wonder about time moving on. "Things, they don't always work out the way that I'd like," Langley sings. "Like how I wish he was still here to hold me tonight." Later she adds, "But I'm movin' on, I'm climbin' that hill. Can't slow down time, but could I make time stand still?"

The soundtrack arrived the same day, with 29 tracks in all. It also includes Noah Kahan's song "Draw You Out," plus music from Noah Cyrus, Bella Kay, Stevie Nicks, Smashing Pumpkins, Violet Grohl, Gigi Perez, and more.

The film opens in theaters on November 20. It is a prequel to the original Hunger Games trilogy and follows a young Haymitch Abernathy, played by Joseph Zada, as he takes part in the 50th Hunger Games. The cast also includes Mckenna Grace, Whitney Peak, Ralph Fiennes, Jesse Plemons, Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin, Kelvin Harrison Jr., Maya Hawke, and Lili Taylor. Francis Lawrence directed the film. He has directed the past four Hunger Games films.

The song caps a busy year for Langley. She released her second album, Dandelion, in April and toured across North America in support of it. Next, she will perform at the 2026 CMA Awards on November 18, where she leads all nominees with nine nominations, including Entertainer of the Year.
why_it_matters: Music shapes how audiences feel about a story before they even see it, and a film soundtrack brings many different artists together around one story. Langley's song also shows how one release can cap a big year for an artist, from a new album and a tour to leading the CMA Award nominations.
